title: Summarize Elements of Effective Security Governance

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Security governance turns leadership direction into rules, responsibilities, and repeatable action. Learn to distinguish governance documents, outside obligations, oversight structures, and data roles.
sections.callout: Policy sets direction; standards define mandatory requirements; procedures explain how work is performed.

entries.title: Guidelines
paragraphs: Recommended practices that allow implementation flexibility.

entries.title: Policies
paragraphs: High-level management statements defining required organizational direction.

entries.title: Standards
paragraphs: Mandatory detailed requirements supporting policy.

entries.title: Procedures
paragraphs: Step-by-step instructions for performing work.

entries.title: Playbooks
paragraphs: Documented action sequences for recurring operational situations.
entries.recognitionCue: If this happens, follow these actions -> Playbook

entries.title: Acceptable use policy (AUP)
paragraphs: Rules governing permitted use of organizational technology.

entries.title: Information security policies
paragraphs: High-level requirements for protecting organizational information.

entries.title: Business continuity policy
paragraphs: Direction for sustaining essential operations during disruption.

entries.title: Disaster recovery policy
paragraphs: Direction for restoring technology after a major interruption.

entries.title: Incident response policy
paragraphs: Direction defining how security incidents must be handled.

entries.title: Software development lifecycle (SDLC) policy
paragraphs: Security requirements throughout software creation and maintenance.

entries.title: Change management policy
paragraphs: Requirements for authorizing, testing, documenting, and controlling changes.

entries.title: Password standard
paragraphs: Mandatory password configuration and handling requirements.

entries.title: Access control standard
paragraphs: Mandatory requirements for granting and reviewing access.

entries.title: Physical security standard
paragraphs: Mandatory facility and equipment protection requirements.

entries.title: Encryption standard
paragraphs: Mandatory cryptographic protection requirements.

entries.title: Change management procedure
paragraphs: Steps to request, approve, test, implement, document, and reverse a change.

entries.title: Onboarding/offboarding procedure
paragraphs: Steps to grant and remove access as personnel join or leave.

entries.title: External considerations
paragraphs: Outside obligations that influence governance decisions.

entries.title: Regulatory
paragraphs: Requirements imposed by an authorized regulator.

entries.title: Legal
paragraphs: Obligations established by law or legal agreement.

entries.title: Industry
paragraphs: Sector-specific expectations and practices.

entries.title: Local/regional
paragraphs: Municipal, state, provincial, or regional requirements.

entries.title: National
paragraphs: Country-level requirements.

entries.title: Global
paragraphs: Requirements spanning countries or jurisdictions.

entries.title: Monitoring and revision
paragraphs: Periodic review and updates keep governance effective as risks, technology, obligations, and business needs change.

entries.title: Types of governance structures
paragraphs: Bodies that direct and oversee security.

entries.title: Boards
paragraphs: Senior governing groups with strategic oversight authority.

entries.title: Committees
paragraphs: Groups assigned collective oversight of defined topics.

entries.title: Government entities
paragraphs: Public authorities that establish or enforce requirements.

entries.title: Centralized/decentralized
paragraphs: Authority may be concentrated in one body or distributed among units.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities for Systems and Data

entries.title: Roles and responsibilities for systems and data
paragraphs: Assignments establish accountability for managing and protecting information assets.

entries.title: Owners
paragraphs: Accountable leaders who decide required protection and access.

entries.title: Controllers
paragraphs: Parties that determine why and how personal data is processed.

entries.title: Processors
paragraphs: Parties that process data on a controller's behalf.

entries.title: Custodians/stewards
paragraphs: Personnel responsible for daily operation, maintenance, protection, and data quality.

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Recommended = guideline; direction = policy; mandatory detail = standard; task steps = procedure
Keep operations running = business continuity; restore technology = disaster recovery
Strategic oversight = board; topic oversight = committee
Controller decides purpose and means; processor acts for the controller
Owner is accountable; custodian or steward provides daily care

sections.title: Objective 5.1 Exam Trap
paragraphs: Policy and procedure are not interchangeable. Business continuity preserves essential operations; disaster recovery restores technology. A controller decides why and how personal data is processed; a processor acts for the controller.
sections.callout: Identify whether the clue describes direction, a mandatory specification, work steps, oversight, or data responsibility.

miniCheck.prompt: Leadership requires every system to use approved encryption algorithms. A separate document gives administrators the exact steps for applying the approved configuration.

fields.label: Document defining the mandatory approved algorithms
Document giving the exact implementation steps

miniCheck.correctFeedback: Correct. The encryption standard defines the mandatory specification, and the procedure explains how administrators implement it.
miniCheck.retryFeedback: Not quite. Separate the mandatory technical specification from the step-by-step instructions.
